title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page sits between pages of an SGA 4-style text on étale fibre functors (Remarque 3.13, §9.4). It is unrelated to them and appears to be a stray sheet of motivic notes, which fits the cote 'Théorie de Galois des motifs'.

(1) A dictionary of three equivalent data, all over Q.
(a) A group T of multiplicative type over Q ('proto-tore' is crossed out and replaced by 'groupe de t.m.') together with a rational point f in T(Q) that is Zariski-dense ('engendrant T (Zar)').
(b) A subgroup M of Q̄* stable under Gal(Q̄/Q). Here M is the image of the character group X*(T) under evaluation at f. Since f is dense, evaluation is injective, so M ≅ X*(T) as a Galois module. Conversely M determines T, and f is the tautological point.
(c) A strictly full subcategory M' of the category of pairs (E, f), with E a finite-dimensional Q-vector space and f a semisimple endomorphism (equivalently, semisimple finite-dimensional Q[X]-modules), stable under ⊗, ⊕ and subobjects. This is the Tannakian side. The subcategory is Rep(T) with f acting, and its 'motivic Galois group' is T, with fundamental element f. M is the set of eigenvalues of all objects.
This is the toy model of the Tannakian category generated by Frobenius, as for motives over F_q.

(2) Extra structure, each item given functorially on both sides.
- A weight cocharacter d: G_m → T, Galois-invariant. Equivalently a homomorphism d*: M → Z, or a grading on M'.
- A Tate-type character ε: T → G_m with ε∘d(λ) = λ^α, i.e. d*(ε*) = α. Equivalently a rank-1 object Λ of M' (the Lefschetz/Tate object).
- The circled note sets q = ε* = ε(f) ∈ M ∩ Q*.

(3) Claim: (a) T/Im d is compact (i.e. its real form is anisotropic) ⇒ (b) q > 0 and |m| = q^{d*(m)/α} for every m in M ⇔ (c) q > 0 and, for every (E, f) in M' of weight i, all eigenvalues of f on E_C have absolute value q^{i/α}.
In other words, the Riemann hypothesis (eigenvalues are Weil q-numbers of weight i) is equivalent to compactness of the group generated by Frobenius modulo the weight torus.

(4) Proof sketch on the page. For (b) ⇔ (c): the eigenvalues of f on weight-i objects are exactly the m in M with d*(m) = i. A crossed-out paragraph sketches (a) ⇒ (b): T' = T°/Im d is a compact R-group, so characters of it take values of absolute value 1 on the image of f.

The correct argument: for χ in X*(T), the character χ^α · ε^{-d*χ} kills Im d. It is therefore a character of the compact group (T/Im d)(R), so its absolute value at f is 1, giving |χ(f)|^α = |q|^{d*χ}. Conversely, M_0 = ker d* = X*(T/Im d) consists of algebraic numbers all of whose conjugates have absolute value 1. Hence complex conjugation acts as -1 on M_0, which is compactness. So the full equivalence holds, with |q| in place of q.
errors: (a) does not imply q>0. Example: T = G_m, d = ε = id, α = 1, f = -p. Then T/Im d is trivial (compact) but q = -p. The correct statement uses |q|, or adds q>0 as an extra hypothesis. This may be why Grothendieck added 'q>0 et' and drew only a one-way arrow from a) to b).
The converse b) ⇒ a) is not indicated, yet it holds via the conjugation argument on ker d*. The page's arrow is weaker than what is true.
Minor: compactness should be understood as the real points of (T/Im d)_R, or of T°/Im d as in the deleted text; T may be disconnected (torsion in M), but this is harmless.

ideas.what: Equivalence between groups of multiplicative type with a Zariski-dense rational point, Galois-stable subgroups of Q̄*, and ⊗-subcategories of (vector space, semisimple endomorphism) pairs
ideas.modern_name: Tannakian category generated by a semisimple endomorphism; Weil-number (pro)torus as the motivic Galois group of the Frobenius
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (Catégories tannakiennes, 1972); Deligne–Milne (1982); Milne, 'Motives over finite fields' (1994); Langlands–Rapoport (1987)
ideas.where_published: Not in Grothendieck's own published texts; the Tannakian program passed into Saavedra's thesis.

ideas.what: Weight grading as a cocharacter d: G_m → T and a Tate object as a character ε with ε∘d = λ^α
ideas.modern_name: Weight homomorphism w: G_m → G_mot and Tate/Lefschetz character; fibre functor with weight grading
ideas.where_published: unsure (cf. Récoltes et Semailles remarks on motivic Galois groups)

ideas.what: Riemann hypothesis for Frobenius eigenvalues ⇔ compactness of the Frobenius-generated group modulo the weight torus
ideas.modern_name: Weil q-numbers ⇔ anisotropy of G/w(G_m); polarization/compactness criterion in Tannakian categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano 1972 (polarized Tannakian categories); Deligne; Milne 1994; Serre's conjectural properties of motivic Galois groups (1994)

missed.claim: A dated (1965) manuscript trace showing Grothendieck had already formulated the Weil-number torus dictionary (Galois-stable subgroups of Q̄* ↔ Tannakian subcategories of endomorphism pairs ↔ group of multiplicative type with a Zariski-dense rational point). It also shows him reformulating the Riemann hypothesis as compactness of T/Im(weight). These results are usually credited to Saavedra, Deligne–Milne, Milne and Langlands–Rapoport in the 1970s–90s.
missed.quote: T/Im d est compact ⇓ q>0 et Pour tout m∈M, on a |m| = q^{d*(m)/α}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical attribution: it documents that the 'compactness modulo weight ⇔ Riemann hypothesis' viewpoint, central to Milne's and Langlands–Rapoport's Weil-number protorus, originates in Grothendieck's 1965 motivic Galois notes. Mathematically, though, it is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is correct (up to a sign issue with q) and now standard, via Saavedra, Deligne–Milne and Milne. It is of mild historical interest as an early, explicit 1965 Grothendieck formulation of the Weil-number torus and of the Riemann hypothesis as a compactness condition.
transcription_corrections: Line a): 'proto-' (in 'proto-tore') is crossed out and 'groupe de t.m.' is written above.
The added phrase 'de rang 1' qualifies the object Λ of M'.
The added 'semi-simple' qualifies 'endomorphismes' and the Q[X]-modules.
In the struck-out paragraph, 'T'=T°/Im d' (with T°) is legible; in item a) the image appears to read 'T/Im d'.
'ε d(λ) = λ^α', i.e. 'd*(ε*)=α', is written at the right margin.
